easy.def: To stay up and not fall over.
examples: I can balance on one foot.
The seal balances a ball on its nose.
Can you balance a book on your head?

more.def: To keep yourself or an object steady so it does not tip or fall.
examples: The gymnast balanced on the narrow beam without wobbling.
He balanced the tray of drinks as he walked across the room.
It is hard to balance on a bike when you first learn to ride.

easy.def: A small animal that flies at night.
examples: A bat flew out of the cave.
Bats sleep in the day.
We saw a bat in the barn.

more.def: A small furry animal with wings that sleeps in the day and flies at night.
examples: The bat hung upside down from the roof of the cave.
A bat can eat hundreds of insects in one night.
Bats use sound to find their way in the dark.

easy.def: A stick you use to hit a ball.
examples: She hit the ball with her bat.
My bat is made of wood.
He left his bat at the park.

more.def: A wooden or metal stick used to hit the ball in games like baseball and cricket.
examples: He swung the bat and sent the ball over the fence.
The coach handed each player a helmet and a bat.
Her new bat is lighter than her old one.

easy.def: To hit something, like a ball.
examples: The cat likes to bat the toy.
It is my turn to bat.
The baby bats at the toy over her crib.

more.def: To hit at something with a bat or with your hand or paw.
examples: The kitten batted the string back and forth.
Our best hitter will bat first in the next game.
She batted the balloon up into the air.

easy.def: Very nice to look at or hear.
examples: What a beautiful flower!
The sunset is beautiful.
You made a beautiful card.

more.def: Very pleasing to see, hear, or think about.
examples: The beautiful music made everyone stop and listen.
The garden looked beautiful after the roses bloomed.
She has a beautiful singing voice.

easy.def: To think that something is true.
examples: I believe you.
I believe it will snow soon.
Do you believe in fairies?

more.def: To feel sure that something is true or real.
examples: She believed her team could win if they worked together.
Nobody believed him when he said he saw a bear.
I believe that practice will make me a better swimmer.
The cat is beneath the table.
The fish swim beneath the boat.
I hid beneath my blanket.
The treasure was buried beneath an old oak tree.
Worms tunnel beneath the surface of the soil.
We sat beneath a shady tree to eat our lunch.

easy.def: A flower on a tree or plant.
examples: The tree has pink blossoms.
A blossom fell on my hand.
Bees like the sweet blossoms.

more.def: A flower, especially one on a tree that will later grow fruit.
examples: In spring, the apple trees are covered in white blossoms.
Cherry blossoms cover the park in pink every April.
Each blossom on the pear tree may turn into a fruit.

easy.def: To use something that is not yours and then give it back.
examples: Can I borrow your red crayon?
I borrow books from my friend.
May I borrow your pencil?

more.def: To take and use something that belongs to someone else, planning to return it.
examples: She borrowed three books from the library and returned them on Friday.
He borrowed his dad's umbrella because it was raining.
You can borrow a board game from the classroom shelf.

easy.def: A line that shows where a place ends.
examples: The fence is the boundary of our yard.
The white line is the boundary of the field.
A wall marks the boundary of the farm.

more.def: A line or edge that marks where one area ends and another begins.
examples: The river forms the boundary between the two countries.
The ball rolled past the boundary, so play stopped.
Mountains form a natural boundary between the two valleys.
The brave girl went down the big slide.
The brave boy got his shot at the doctor.
Firefighters are brave.

more.def: Willing to do something hard or scary even when you feel afraid.
examples: It was brave of him to speak in front of the whole school.
The brave sailor steered the ship through the storm.
She was brave enough to say sorry first.
A cool breeze blew my hair.
The breeze moved the curtains.
My kite flew in the breeze.
A breeze from the sea kept us cool on the hot beach.
The flags waved gently in the morning breeze.
We opened the windows to let the breeze in.
The sun is very bright.
I wear a bright yellow coat.
The lamp is too bright for my eyes.

more.def: Giving off or filled with a lot of light; also, strong in color.
examples: The bright moon lit up the whole field.
Bright stars filled the sky on the clear night.
She painted her room a bright shade of green.

easy.def: A group of things tied together.
examples: Dad had a bundle of sticks.
Mom gave me a bundle of clean socks.
The baby is in a bundle of blankets.

more.def: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
examples: She carried a bundle of newspapers under her arm.
He tied the old letters in a bundle with string.
The farmer stacked bundles of hay in the barn.

easy.def: A hole in the ground where an animal lives.
examples: The rabbit ran into its burrow.
A mole lives in a burrow.
The snake hid in a burrow.

more.def: A hole or tunnel that an animal digs in the ground to live in.
examples: The fox kept her cubs safe in a burrow under the hill.
Prairie dogs dig burrows with many rooms.
The owl made its nest in an empty burrow.
